properties.name: Harappa
properties.notes: Eponymous type site of the Harappan civilization; on the Ravi. Excavated 1920-21 to 1933-34 (Vats) and 1986-2001 (HARP).
sources: Vats, M.S. 1940. Excavations at Harappa, Vol. I (text), Vol. II (139 plates). Govt. of India Press. — title page (site name); Plate I (site plan; georeferenced for coordinates and mound polygons)

IGNOU eGyankosh BHIC-101E Unit 5 (Dr. Avantika Sharma): 'Harappa was excavated in 1920 by Daya Ram Sahni'; 'following the archaeological convention of naming a culture where it was first discovered'; chronology table lists Harappa under Early (3300-2600 BCE), Mature (2600-1800 BCE), Late ('Cemetery H at Harappa')

Harappa Archaeological Research Project (HARP), harappa.com/indus4/e1.html: Period 1 Ravi/Hakra (>3500-2800 BC), Period 2 Kot Diji (2800-2600 BC), Period 3 Harappa phase (2600-1900 BC), Period 5 Late Harappa (c.1800-<1300 BC)
Kenoyer 2008 (Sackler Colloquium, harappa.com PDF): city grew to 150 ha in the Harappa phase; Dales & Kenoyer 1990: areal extent ~150 ha; Vats 1940:3: site ~3.5 miles 'in circuit'
properties.authority_note: All fields traced to excavation report, excavation project, or national university course material.

properties.name: Dholavira
properties.notes: Tripartite fortified Harappan city (citadel, middle town, lower town) with elaborate reservoir-based water harvesting; ten large Indus-script gypsum inlays ("signboard") at the North Gate. Excavated 1989-90 to 2004-05 (ASI, R.S. Bisht).
sources: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: 'Dholavira: A Harappan City', inscribed 2021, 44COM 8B.35, ref. 1645 — official property name
UNESCO nomination table, doc 187795 (properties examined 2021): centre point N23 53 18.27 E70 12 47.89 (= 23.8884, 70.2133); inscribed area 103 ha

Bisht, R.S. 2015. Excavations at Dholavira (1989-2005). ASI — reservoirs (§pp.148,164 per public copy); signboard (§8.1.1, pp.228-231 per public copy); seven cultural stages, occupation through 3rd millennium into mid-2nd millennium BCE

Bisht lecture, IIT Gandhinagar, 18 Oct 2013 ('Dholavira: A Unique Harappan City'): 13 field seasons 1989-90 to 2004-05; 'one amongst five largest urban centers of Harappan civilization' (with Mohenjodaro, Harappa, Ganweriwala, Rakhigarhi)
IGNOU eGyankosh BHIC-101E Unit 5: Dholavira among Gujarat Harappan sites; listed under Mature Harappan and in Transitional Phase row

properties.harappan_connection: One Indus stamp seal with elephant (probably made in Indus region, traded to Gonur); abundant ivory; artifacts with Indus stylistic traits (Sarianidi excavations, per Penn Museum Expedition Magazine).
properties.name: Gonur Tepe
properties.notes: BMAC (Oxus civilization) capital in Margiana, Turkmenistan. Key evidence for Indus-Central Asia contact.
sources: Penn Museum Expedition Magazine, 'The Middle Asian Interaction Sphere': 'one very fine Indus stamp seal with an elephant... probably made in the Indus region and brought or traded to Gonur' (Sarianidi excavations)
Discover Magazine: Indus Valley stamp with etched elephant found at Gonur
